messages:
Sam H: Heads-up — we need to coordinate a base-image rebuild that changes the KMS key wrapping policy and adds a new audit field (kms_key_id) to container start events. Planning window: tomorrow 02:00 PT. Will likely increase audit events; need RBAC checks for runtime agents and the audit-pipeline schema update. Any immediate red flags?

Vivian L: +1 on needing the schema bump. Audit pipeline will choke if we don't version the payloads. Can we make the new field optional for 48h?

Sam H: Yes, plan is opt-in by default for the first 24h, then flip to required after canary. But runtime will start sending kms_key_id when present.

Ash K: Two operational things: 1) runtime service account needs decrypt permissions on the new key for ephem logs signing? 2) Image signer (cosign) workflow will switch to the new key alias; IAM role name will change. We should validate cluster RBAC & KMS IAM before the flip.

Maria S: Who owns the KMS policy changes? I can take the IAM gating if Sec-ops signs off. Also remind: audit retention rules may need bumping if event volume goes up.

Sam H: Maria, thanks. Can you own the key ACL & role grant. Ash — can you run a dry RBAC test in staging? I can coordinate canary.

Ash K: Running a quick dry-check against staging now. Command I used: 
```
# list key bindings (gcp example)
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/new-rebuild-key --format=json
```
One thing: runtime agents use Workload Identity. We need to ensure the KSA -> GSA mapping includes the iamroles/decrypt binding.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for tag image-rebuild:v3-canary in cluster staging-us-west-2. 4 pods scheduled, 2 healthy, 2 pending (node selectors).

Vivian L: sec-oncall, any concerns about incidentability? If we change the audit schema mid-rollout, oncall alerts for missing fields might trigger false positives. We should add suppression rule for the first 6 hours.

sec-oncall: Agreed — please open a suppression ticket. I'll watch the alert stream. Also, add a logshipper mapping for the new field: 
```
logstash { if [kubernetes][container][kms_key_id] { mutate { add_field => { "kms_key_id" => "%{[kubernetes][container][kms_key_id]}" } } }
```
I'll coordinate with Observability to accept the optional field.

Maria S: IAM snippet I'll roll to the infra repo: 
```
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding" "runtime_decrypt" {
  crypto_key_id = "projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/new-rebuild-key"
  role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
  members       = ["serviceAccount:project-staging-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
}
```
I'll open a PR and tag @Ash K and @Sam H for review.

Ash K: Staging dry-run logs show runtime agents can reach KMS and cosign verification uses the old key as fallback. Two minor errors: 1) one node pool missing IAM annotation; 2) one canary pod had permission denied on reading /var/log/containermeta. Fixes queued.

Sam H: Good catch. Let's keep the fallback window for another 6 hours after initial canary success. Sequence for tomorrow: 
1) Maria applies IAM binding in prod-staging.
2) Ash runs a non-disruptive smoke (15m).
3) Deploy canary to prod small pool (2 pods).
4) Wait 30m, check audit pipeline & alert suppression.
5) Flip opt-in -> required after 24h if no issues.

Vivian L: I'll create the alert suppression ticket and update the audit schema docs. Link to runbook: https://internal.redwood.dev/runbooks/audit-schema-migrations (please review).

sec-oncall: I'll be on standby during the prod canary window. If alerts spike or if we see >1% pod startup failures referencing kms_key_id, we roll back.

Sam H: Thanks everyone. PR links + canary results here when ready. :rocket:
